title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: YOLANDA'S BEES
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Yolanda, who runs a raisin packing line in Fresno, California.
She fears exactly one thing. Bees.
So of course, her Uncle Rudy left her sixty thousand of them.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE BOXES
segments.quote: The great end of life is not knowledge but action.
segments.author: Thomas Henry Huxley
lines: Rudy retired to Arizona and left four hives in her backyard.
Yolanda read five library books on bees. From the kitchen window.
Rudy called and read her a line from Thomas Huxley, an English scientist:
The great end of life is not knowledge but action.
So she bought a veil and gloves up to her elbows, and walked outside.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE STING
segments.quote: Our business in this world is not to succeed, but to continue to fail, in good spirits.
segments.author: Robert Louis Stevenson
lines: She yanked the first lid open like a jammed machine. A bee stung her on the nose.
Her friend Ofelia taped a line from Robert Louis Stevenson to her locker:
Our business in this world is not to succeed, but to continue to fail, in good spirits.
So Yolanda laughed and went back out. Band-Aid on the nose.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: SLOW HANDS
segments.quote: Whoever is in a hurry shows that the thing he is about is too big for him.
segments.author: Lord Chesterfield
lines: Bees hate fast moves. Yolanda did everything fast.
Rudy quoted Lord Chesterfield, who wrote his son letters full of advice:
Whoever is in a hurry shows that the thing he is about is too big for him.
So she went slow. A whole month, not one sting.
At the plant, she quit yelling hurry up. The line ran smoother.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE SWARM
segments.quote: He that has once done you a kindness will be more ready to do you another, than he whom you yourself have obliged.
segments.author: Benjamin Franklin
lines: One June morning, half the bees swarmed into grumpy Mr. Petrosyan's fig tree next door.
She remembered Ben Franklin's trick for winning over a grump. Ask him a favor.
He that has once done you a kindness will be more ready to do you another, than he whom you yourself have obliged.
So she borrowed his ladder. He held it while she caught the swarm. Now he brings her figs on Sundays.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE HONEY
segments.quote: No one has ever become poor from giving.
segments.author: Anne Frank
lines: In August, she pulled forty pounds of honey. She planned to sell every jar.
Then she saw Rudy's old fridge magnet, with words from Anne Frank, the young diary writer:
No one has ever become poor from giving.
So she gave jars to the packing line, and to Mr. Petrosyan. He teared up. He says it was pollen.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE GARDEN
segments.author: Voltaire
lines: Soon the neighbors asked what they could plant for the bees.
Yolanda thought of the last line of Candide, by the French writer Voltaire:
Let us cultivate our garden.
So she ripped out her dead lawn, planted lavender, and handed out seeds door to door.
Now Olive Avenue hums. Yolanda still screams at flies. Never at bees.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Act. Laugh it off. Slow down. Ask a favor. Give. Plant something.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Stop reading and start. Laugh at the sting. Slow down. Ask a favor. Give it away. Plant something.
I got stung once myself. I tell everyone it's a dueling scar.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
